item.content:encoded:
from: One corporation to pollute them all

In April, Ecohustler disrupted Carnival Cruise’s AGM calling on the shareholders to reduce their company’s pollution using straight forward and affordable methods - like burning cleaner fuel. Since then, a new report outlines the corporation’s impact on the coastline of Europe. These vast floating cities are burning dirty bunker fuel and creating shocking levels of air pollution wherever they go. Shipping has been an unregulated industry for too long and action is urgently required.

今年 4 月，Ecohustler 干扰了 Carnival Cruise 的股东大会，呼吁股东们利用简单且经济实惠的方法（如燃烧更清洁的燃料）来减少公司污染。自那时起，一份新报告概述了该公司对欧洲海岸线的影响。这些巨大的“海上漂浮城市”燃烧肮脏的船用重油，所到之处造成令人震惊的空气污染水平。航运业长期处于无监管状态，亟需采取行动。

Carnival Corporation, the world’s largest luxury cruise operator, emitted nearly 10 times more sulphur oxide (SOx) around European coasts than did all 260 million European cars in 2017, a new analysis by sustainable transport group Transport & Environment reveals.

Carnival Corporation，全球最大的豪华邮轮运营商，在 2017 年环绕欧洲海岸时排放的硫氧化物（SOx）量几乎是所有 260 百万辆欧洲汽车总量的 10 倍，一项由可持续交通组织 Transport & Environment 发布的 new analysis 证实了这一数据。

Royal Caribbean Cruises, the world’s second largest, is second, yet four times worse than the European car fleet. SOx emissions form sulphate (SO4) aerosols that increase human health risks and contribute to acidification in terrestrial and aquatic environments.

皇家加勒比邮轮（Royal Caribbean Cruises）作为全球第二大邮轮公司排名第二，但其（SOx 排放）比整个欧洲的汽车车队还要严重四倍。

SOx 排放会形成硫酸盐（SO4）气溶胶，从而增加人类健康风险，并导致陆地和水域环境的酸化。

In absolute terms, Spain, Italy and Greece, closely followed by France and Norway, are the European countries most exposed to SOx air pollution from cruise vessels while Barcelona, Palma de Mallorca and Venice are the most impacted European port cities, followed by Civitavecchia (Rome) and Southampton.

就绝对量而言 Spain, Italy and Greece, 紧随 France and Norway 之后，欧洲国家最易受 SOx 大气污染的游轮影响，而 Barcelona, Palma de Mallorca and Venice 是最受影响的欧洲港口城市，随后是 Civitavecchia (Rome) and Southampton。

All photos by Greg English ©

所有照片由 Greg English 拍摄 ©

These countries are so exposed because they are major tourist destinations, but also because they have less stringent marine sulphur fuel standards which allows cruise ships to burn the dirtiest most sulphurous fuel all along their coastlines.

这些国家如此暴露，因为它们是主要的旅游目的地，但也因为它们有更宽松的海洋硫燃料标准，允许游轮在其海岸线上燃烧最脏、硫含量最高的燃料。

Faig Abbasov, shipping policy manager at T&E, said: “Luxury cruise ships are floating cities powered by some of the dirtiest fuel possible. Cities are rightly banning dirty diesel cars but they’re giving a free pass to cruise companies that spew out toxic fumes that do immeasurable harm both to those on board and on nearby shores. This is unacceptable.“

Faig Abbasov，T&E 的航运政策经理表示：“豪华邮轮是使用最肮脏燃料驱动的漂浮城市。城市正确地禁止肮脏的柴油车，却对排放有毒烟雾的邮轮公司大开方便之门；这些烟雾对船上人员和附近海岸造成了无法估量的伤害。这是不可接受的。”

NOX emissions from cruise ships in Europe also heavily impact some cities, equivalent to about 15% of the nitrogen oxides (NOx) emitted by Europe’s passenger car fleet in a year, the report finds. In Marseille, for example, 57 cruise ships emitted in 2017 almost as much NOx as one-quarter of the city’s 340,000 passenger cars. Along the coasts of countries such as Norway, Denmark, Greece, Croatia and Malta a handful of cruise ships are also responsible for more NOx than the majority of their domestic car fleet.

报告显示，欧洲邮轮的 NOx 排放同样对部分城市造成严重影响，约相当于欧洲乘用车车队一年排放的氮氧化物（NOx）的 15%。例如，2017 年，马赛港的 57 艘邮轮排放的 NOx 几乎相当于该市 34 万辆乘用车排放量的四分之一。在挪威、丹麦、希腊、克罗地亚和马耳他等国沿海，少数几艘邮轮排放的 NOx 也超过这些国家本国乘用车车队大部分车辆的排放量。

Europe should implement a zero-emission port standard as soon as possible, this could then be extended to other ship types. The report also recommends extending emission control areas (ECAs), currently in place only in the North and Baltic Seas and English Channel, to the rest of the European seas. Furthermore, the report recommends regulating NOx emissions from existing ships, which are currently exempt from NOx standards applying in emission control areas.

欧洲应当应尽快实施零排放港口标准，这可以随后扩展到其他船舶类型。报告还建议将排放控制区（ ECA ）扩展到欧洲其他海域。目前，这些区域仅在北海和波罗的海以及英吉利海峡生效。此外，报告还建议监管现有船舶的 NOx 排放，而这些船舶目前被豁免适用于排放控制区域的 NOx 标准。

Faig Abbasov concluded “There are enough mature technologies to clean up cruise ships. Shore-side electricity can help cut in-port emissions, batteries are a solution for shorter distances and hydrogen technology can power even the biggest cruise ships. The cruise sector are apparently not willing to make the shift voluntarily, so we need governments to step in and mandate zero emission standards.”

Faig Abbasov 总结道：“已经有足够成熟的技术可以清洁邮轮。岸电可以帮助减少港口排放，电池是短距离航行的解决方案，而氢能技术甚至可以为最大的邮轮提供动力。邮轮行业显然不愿意主动做出转变，因此我们需要政府介入，强制推行零排放标准。”

item.title: 禁止移动操作系统平台中AI代理捕获数据
item.description:
Privacy is our mission; it’s why we exist, and we do everything we can to protect it.

隐私是我们的使命；这是我们存在的原因，我们尽一切努力保护它。

This means that we are restricting the latest AI agents built into mobile operating systems from potentially capturing and storing your Signal data.
item.content:encoded:
from: Signal is Serious About Protecting Your Privacy

Privacy is our mission; it’s why we exist, and we do everything we can to protect it.

隐私是我们的使命；这是我们存在的原因，我们尽一切努力保护它。

This means that we are restricting the latest AI agents built into mobile operating systems from potentially capturing and storing your Signal data.

这意味着我们正在限制移动操作系统中内置的最新 AI 代理，以防止其可能捕获和存储你的 Signal 数据。

We’ve already had to do this once with Windows. Last year, we used screenshot blocking to prevent Microsoft’s Recall AI from taking and storing screenshots of your Signal messages on Windows 11 operating systems by default.1 We will now be taking similar measures to restrict agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where we can detect an AI assistant attempting to read your Signal screen.2

我们已经不得不在 Windows 上这样做过一次。去年，我们使用截图阻止功能来 prevent Microsoft 的 Recall AI 在 Windows 11 操作系统中默认拍摄和存储你的 Signal 消息的截图。1 我们现在将采取类似措施，限制内置于 iOS 27 以及我们能检测到 AI 助手试图读取你 Signal 屏幕的 Android 版本上的 agentic 系统。2

The problem is similar to Microsoft Recall on Windows: Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems. This is a significant move. Google (Android), Apple (iOS/macOS), and Microsoft (Windows) produce the three major consumer operating systems (OS), which comprise the environment that third-party developers – like Signal – build their apps to function and operate within. To put it differently, these three operating systems are the oceans in which Signal, and other applications, must swim; they dictate the conditions of life for the application ecosystem. Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy. This is an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission.

这一问题类似于 Windows 上的 Microsoft Recall：Google 和 Apple 正将诸如 Gemini Intelligence（搭配 Google Gemini）和 Onscreen Awareness（搭配 Siri AI）这类代理能力深度集成到其操作系统中。这是一个重大举措。Google（Android）、Apple（iOS/macOS）和 Microsoft（Windows）构建了三大主流消费级操作系统（OS），第三方开发者（如 Signal）正是在这些环境中构建并运行其应用。换个说法，这三大操作系统是 Signal 等应用赖以生存的海洋；它们决定了应用生态系统的生存条件。目前，这些代理式 AI 集成正在以一种日益对隐私不利的方式改变这一环境。这对 Signal 构成了生存威胁，也威胁到我们负责任地坚守使命的能力。

In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents “scan” the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding.

为了获取关于你的信息，这些 OS AI 代理 “扫描” 你屏幕上的信息。在此过程中， 你的 Signal 数据被捕获， 然后提供给这些 agentic 系统， 以便它们能够回答你的问题并执行你的指令。

The net result is that these AI capabilities in the operating system are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy. For over a decade, this guarantee has been backed by our tried and trusted open source code base and our formally verified encryption protocol. These have been scrutinized by some of the best security experts and hackers across the world, and shown to be robust. Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment. All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.

净结果是，操作系统中的这些 AI 功能正在削弱 Signal 独立保障隐私的能力。十多年来，这一保障一直由我们经过验证、值得信赖的开源代码库和形式化验证的加密协议提供支撑。这些代码和协议经受了全球顶尖安全专家和黑客的审视，并被证明是稳健的。如今，为了服务于 AI Agentic 能力，您的敏感数据正在被捕获、存储，并变得可被操作系统级 AI Agent 当时所使用的任何本地数据库或远程服务器访问。一旦数据被捕获，所有这些都将脱离 Signal 的控制，并危及对话中所有参与者的隐私。

So, we are blocking such capture by preventing screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android.[^2:1]

所以，我们通过在 iOS 27 的应用中防止截图，并在 AI 助手尝试在 Android 上捕获屏幕数据时进行阻止。 [^2:1]

People who want the ability to take screenshots can disable this protection within the Signal app’s settings. However, doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees. Our remedy is also incomplete – while we are doing everything we can, restricting screenshots does not address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data, such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.

希望保留截屏功能的用户可以在 Signal 应用设置中关闭此保护。但这样做可能会使您（以及您的联系人）的 Signal 内容暴露给这些 AI Agent，从而破坏我们的隐私保障。我们的补救措施也并不完整——尽管我们已竭尽全力，但限制截屏并不能解决 AI Agent 可能访问应用数据的其他更隐蔽的方式，例如通过文件系统获取用户设备上已有的内容。

We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy. Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS.3

我们想非常明确地说明：Signal——以及 Signal 之外的应用开发者——缺乏可靠的工具来防止 AI Agent 破坏应用层隐私，这是一个严重的问题。即使我们能够检测并阻止 AI 数据访问，Google、Apple、Microsoft 等公司也没有为开发者提供方法，让他们能够在不严重损害核心用户体验的情况下轻松限制此类 AI 数据访问。这也是我们目前无法在 macOS 上实施这些保护措施的原因。3

We are also struggling with a significant lack of documentation about how these AI agents actually work. Over the past few months, we’ve spent considerable developer time and energy doing forensic investigations across Android and iOS in an attempt to learn what is actually happening when these AI systems access application data. Without better documentation and clear technical specifications, it will be increasingly difficult for Signal to provide robust privacy and security to the many millions of people who rely on us.

我们也在应对严重的文档不足问题，这些文档未能解释这些 AI agents 的实际运作方式。过去几个月里，我们花费了大量的开发者时间和精力，在 Android 和 iOS 平台上进行取证调查，试图了解 AI systems 访问应用数据时实际发生的事情。没有更好的文档和清晰的技术规格，Signal 越来越难向依赖我们的数以千万计的用户提供有力的隐私和安全。

We continue to call on the major consumer operating system companies – Apple, Google, and Microsoft – to provide simple technical tools and accurate documentation that give developers like Signal ways to prevent AI agents from accessing sensitive application data. In particular, we are calling on these companies to provide two common-sense remedies that can protect the privacy so many millions of people rely on:

我们继续呼吁 Apple、Google 和 Microsoft 等主要消费级操作系统公司提供简单的技术工具和准确的文档，使像 Signal 这样的开发者能够防止 AI agents 访问敏感应用数据。我们特别呼吁这些公司提供两项常识性补救措施，以保护数千万人依赖的隐私。

  1. Developers should have an easy and well-documented way to opt their app out of AI data access and processing, including (but not limited to) screen reading, filesystem access, notifications, APIs, and other OS frameworks, all without undermining the core utility of an application.
  2. Operating system companies should create better documentation and technical specifications around how these AI agents function, particularly regarding data access and processing. Confidential computing approaches are not a complete solution, and do not address these core concerns. In particular, these approaches still leave the power to determine the extent of privacy guarantees (if any) in the hands of these providers.

  1. 开发人员应拥有一种简单且有完善文档记录的方式，使其应用能够选择退出 AI 数据访问和处理，包括（但不限于）屏幕读取、文件系统访问、通知、API 以及其他 OS 框架，同时不损害应用的核心功能。

  2. 操作系统公司应针对这些 AI 代理的运作方式（特别是在数据访问和处理方面）编制更完善的文档和技术规范。机密计算方法并非完整的解决方案，也无法解决这些核心问题。特别是，这些方法仍然将决定隐私保障程度（如果存在的话）的权力掌握在这些提供商手中。

We also see a growing need for tools that can prevent third-party agents, like Meta’s Muse, from accessing application data using the deep permissions that users are encouraged to grant them during setup. In many cases these agents are leveraging accessibility settings that were meant to empower actual people to get the most out of their apps and services, not to act as a skeleton key that provides access to AI agents.

我们也看到，亟需能够防止第三方 agents 如 Meta 的 Muse 利用用户在设置过程中被鼓励授予的深度权限访问应用数据的工具。在很多情况下，这些 agents 正在利用无障碍设置，而这些设置的初衷是帮助实际用户充分利用其应用和服务，而不是作为向 AI agents 提供访问权限的万能钥匙。

In addition to taking these technical measures to block capture, we are engaging in conversations across the ecosystem to make the stakes clear. There is a lot of work to be done in the industry to improve the ways that AI agents operate in the operating system, and how and whether they capture and process private data. We are cautiously optimistic that some major OS providers, like Google and Apple, are engaging with us on how these systems should better interface with privacy-sensitive apps like Signal. We hope to have more to share on this topic soon, and that these companies recognize the danger to the ecosystem and work with us and others to create standardized approaches that meaningfully protect privacy across the industry.

除了采取这些技术措施来阻止数据捕获，我们还在生态系统中开展对话，以明确风险。行业仍有大量工作要做，以改善 AI Agent 在操作系统中的运行方式，以及它们是否以及如何捕获和处理私有数据。我们对一些大型 OS 提供商，如 Google 和 Apple，就这些系统如何更好地与像 Signal 这样的隐私敏感应用接口表示谨慎乐观。我们希望很快就此主题有更多内容可以分享，并且这些公司能认识到对生态系统的危险，并与我们和其他人合作，创建能够真正保护整个行业隐私的标准化方法。

Finally, we want to acknowledge that we are not the only ones recognizing these perils, and we are grateful to our allies for pushing for similar changes. We all need to recognize that the current integration of AI agents into the operating system, without these common-sense remedies, represents an existential threat to privacy at the application layer, and the ability of independent developers like Signal to protect your sensitive data. Signal is the canary in the coal mine, but this affects the entire ecosystem and should galvanize anyone who cares about these fundamental rights.

最后，我们承认我们并不是唯一认识到这些危机的人，我们感谢我们的盟友推动类似 改变。我们所有人都需要认识到，当前将 AI 代理集成到操作系统中，若没有这些常识性对策，代表着对应用层隐私的生存性威胁，也影响像 Signal 这样的独立开发者保护您的敏感数据的能力。Signal 是煤矿中的警示鸟，但这影响整个生态系统，应激励关心这些基本权利的人。

没有提供需要翻译的英文原文，请粘贴英文原文或发送包含原文的 markdown 文件路径。

Signal Technology Foundation is the nonprofit home of the Signal app, which is trusted by millions around the world. We protect free expression and enable secure global communication through open source privacy technology. Signal Technology Foundation is a US 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization.

Signal Technology Foundation 是 Signal app 的非营利机构，后者受到全球数百万用户的信任。我们通过开源隐私技术保护言论自由，并实现安全的全球通信。Signal Technology Foundation 是一家美国 501(c)(3) 免税组织。

  1. Microsoft Recall captures your screen every few seconds, extracts text from screenshots via optical character recognition, then populates a searchable on-device database with this personal data in order to allow the AI system to query it – potentially exposing and retaining your Signal data indefinitely, including disappearing messages. ↩︎ ↩︎

  2. There are multiple versions of Android beyond the Google-provided distributions on Pixel devices. For many vendors, we don’t have a reliable way to detect when a screenshot was attempted if screenshots are already disabled. Rather than choose a poor user experience (where screenshots simply stop working, confusing users), we decided to instead focus on detecting when an AI assistant attempts to access the screen. We automatically enable the “Screen security” setting in Signal Android when this type of access is detected. ↩︎ ↩︎

  3. Careful readers will note that in addition to not being able to cover all Android devices, we are also not blocking Siri AI on macOS. This is because we cannot reliably block screenshots on macOS. Faced with a lack of clearly documented APIs that allow us to implement screenshot protection, we do not have the tools available that let us do the job. While protections against continuous screen capture exist on macOS, we cannot apply them to screenshots (which is how most agentic systems access data from applications like Signal). Trying to implement screenshot blocking on macOS has revealed to us a minefield of bewildering decisions that place user privacy at risk, including APIs that have been deprecated in favor of screen-protection solutions that only work for streaming media and other DRM-protected content. This is something we hope Apple remedies urgently. For now, the only recommendation we have for macOS 27 users is to add Signal to the Excluded Apps section in System Settings > Siri to protect message content from proactive access by Siri AI. ↩︎ ↩︎

item.title: 这个标题里的 CVE 编号和年份看起来像是虚构的。不过，标题的意思是：OpenSSL 的 EVP_EncodeBlock() 函数存在缓冲区溢出漏洞。如果你需要翻译，可以参考这个版本：“OpenSSL：EVP_EncodeBlock() 函数中的缓冲区溢出漏洞”。
item.description:
This fixes “Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock()” (CVE-2026-121481) by returning -1 for invalid inputs to EVP_EncodeBlock(): NULL input or output buffers, negative lengths, and lengths for which the encoded size does not fit in an int. The OpenSSL SRT has asked for it to be fixed publicly; the advisory is still pending.

此修复 EVP_EncodeBlock() 中的缓冲区溢出 (CVE-2026-121481 “CVE-2026-121481”)) by 返回 -1： NULL 输入或输出缓冲区、负长度以及长度超出 int 范围的情况。 OpenSSL SRT 已要求公开修复；该 advisory 仍在等待。
item.content:encoded:
from: [NSF] [CVE-2026-121481] Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() by nmouha · Pull Request #33652 · openssl/openssl · GitHub

This fixes “Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock()” (CVE-2026-121481) by returning -1 for invalid inputs to EVP_EncodeBlock(): NULL input or output buffers, negative lengths, and lengths for which the encoded size does not fit in an int. The OpenSSL SRT has asked for it to be fixed publicly; the advisory is still pending.

此修复 EVP_EncodeBlock() 中的缓冲区溢出 (CVE-2026-121481 “CVE-2026-121481”)) by 返回 -1： NULL 输入或输出缓冲区、负长度以及长度超出 int 范围的情况。 OpenSSL SRT 已要求公开修复；该 advisory 仍在等待。

Returning -1 for invalid inputs is the most straightforward fix, and matches what happens in wolfSSL’s compatibility layer for OpenSSL’s EVP_EncodeBlock().

对无效输入返回 -1 是最直接的修复方案，并且与 wolfSSL’s compatibility layer for OpenSSL’s EVP_EncodeBlock() 的行为一致。

I’m suggesting a similar guard for EVP_DecodeBlock(). No length limit is needed here because the decoded length always fits in an int, but it is a good idea to reject NULL buffers and negative lengths.

我建议为 EVP_DecodeBlock() 添加类似的保护措施。这里不需要限制长度， 因为解码后的长度始终能够放入 int ， 但建议拒绝 NULL 缓冲区和负长度。

Moreover, I propose to fix the incorrect length check in the base64encode() function of http_client.c, which rejected only len > INT_MAX.

此外，我提议修复 http_client.c 中 base64encode() 函数的不当长度检查，该检查仅拒绝了 len > INT_MAX。

I am adding tests in test/base64_dec_avx2_test.c to cover the new behavior, and documenting the -1 returns in doc/man3/EVP_EncodeInit.pod.

我正在向 test/base64_dec_avx2_test.c 添加测试，以覆盖新行为，并在 doc/man3/EVP_EncodeInit.pod 中文档化 -1 返回值。

Exploiting this vulnerability from the command line is possible by passing a large -proxy_pass to openssl s_client. I confirmed that GOST accepts these large passwords out of the box. However, the password has to be supplied through an environment variable (env:VAR), otherwise the command line will be too long.

from: Introducing Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed, and verified end-to-end by AI

Abstract

摘要

In our previous post, Redwood, we showed that given an architecture, our AI systems could implement, verify, and deploy an inference accelerator in record time. However, similar to other scientific domains, we believe that AI systems, given the correct freedom and guardrails, can co-design software and hardware together, making optimizations across the stack and opening a design space so large it was previously inaccessible. We set out to answer the question: “Could our AI systems & tools lead to a novel hardware discovery that radically outperforms human-made designs?”

Introduction to interaction nets

Interaction nets 简介

Mainstream programming languages, when compiled for general-purpose CPUs, hide the dependencies between the parts of a program. Any piece of code may read or write any variable through a shared, mutable state, and so modern CPU hardware assumes the worst case and rediscovers, at runtime, which instructions actually depend on each other. Moreover, single-core CPU performance has largely stalled since the early 2000s, pushing people towards large multicore CPUs such as Intel Xeon, AMD Zen, and NVIDIA Vera. This forces CPUs to maintain the illusion that every core sees the same memory, and keeping that illusion consistent and performant requires deep cache hierarchies and coherence protocols that cost area and power, and scale poorly.

主流编程语言在编译为通用 CPU 时，会隐藏程序各部分之间的依赖关系。任何代码都可能通过共享的可变状态来读取或写入任何变量，因此现代 CPU 硬件会假设最坏情况，并在运行时重新发现哪些指令实际上相互依赖。此外，单核 CPU 性能自 2000 年代初以来基本停滞，推动人们转向大型多核 CPU，例如 Intel Xeon、AMD Zen 和 NVIDIA Vera。这迫使 CPU 维持每个核心都能看到相同内存的错觉，而保持这一错觉的一致性和性能需要深层次缓存层次结构和一致性协议，这些会消耗面积和功耗，并且难以扩展。

Interaction nets1 take a different approach. A program is a graph of nodes, and computation happens by rewriting pairs of nodes that are connected through their ports. Every rewrite only touches a small, local part of the graph. Because each node has exactly one principal port, no two of these active pairs ever overlap, so they can be rewritten in any order, or all at once, and the result is always the same. Interaction nets are also linear: every value is used exactly once, so there is no shared mutable state for the hardware to guard. Languages such as Vine2 compile ordinary-looking programs directly to interaction nets. For an excellent introduction to interaction nets and why they suit hardware, we highly recommend Tendrils’ “On Interaction Nets.” 3

Interaction nets1 采用了不同的方法。程序是一个节点图，计算通过重写通过端口连接的节点对来实现。每次重写只触及图的一小部分局部。因为每个节点都只有一个主端口，所以这些活动对不会重叠；它们可以以任何顺序重写，或一次性重写，并且结果总是相同的。Interaction nets 也是线性的：每个值正好被使用一次，因此没有共享可变状态需要硬件守护。诸如 Vine2 这样的语言会直接将看起来普通的程序编译成 interaction nets。我们强烈推荐 Tendrils 的《On Interaction Nets》作为对 interaction nets 及其为什么适合硬件的极好介绍.3

In theory, this should have two large advantages. The first is multithreading for free: rather than varying levels of coarse and fine-grained parallelism, parallelism comes straight from the program. No threads, locks, or race conditions, and none of the out-of-order machinery a conventional core uses to dig it back out. The second is that, since every value has one owner and every step is local, data can live in small local memories next to where it is used. That removes much of the area and power a conventional chip spends on large caching subsystems, and much of the system-level complexity of keeping those caches coherent.

理论上，这应具有两大显著优势。首先是免费获得多线程能力：并行性直接源自程序本身，而非依赖粗粒度和细粒度并行程度不一的显式管理。无需线程、锁，也不存在竞态条件，更不需要传统核心用于从指令流中重新挖掘并行性的乱序执行机制。其次，由于每个值仅有一个所有者且每个步骤均为局部操作，数据可驻留在靠近使用位置的小型局部存储中。这消除了传统芯片在大型缓存子系统上投入的大量面积和功耗，也大幅降低了维护缓存一致性所带来的系统级复杂性。

Formal contracts and system modeling

形式合同与系统建模

Once the architecture candidate was selected, our system moved on to building the full software model of the chip. Building software models is essential when exploring an architectural space, as they allow fast iteration between the workloads, the ISA, and the abstracted view of the hardware. Whether we build a CPU, GPU, NPU, or networking switch, mastering this iteration loop allows the fastest exploration of the design space within a finite time. To do this repeatedly, we designed a new in-house specification language, ASL, and wrote Frostbite’s system model “Arcmodel” in it. ASL supports machine-checkable translations and refinements between RTL, system models, UVM, SVA, and more, all against a formally backed specification. Its power and performance estimates are accurate to within 1–5%, it runs roughly 200x faster than RTL simulation, and it is formally verifiable through “contracts.”

架构候选选定后，我们的系统转向构建芯片的完整软件模型。在探索架构空间时，构建软件模型至关重要，因为它们允许在工作负载、ISA 和硬件抽象视图之间进行快速迭代。无论我们构建 CPU、GPU、NPU 还是网络交换机，掌握这个迭代循环都能在有限时间内实现对设计空间的最快探索。为了反复进行此操作，我们设计了全新的自家规格语言 ASL，并将 Frostbite 的系统模型 “Arcmodel” 写入其中。ASL 支持在 RTL、系统模型、UVM、SVA 以及更多之间进行机器可检查的翻译和细化，全部基于正式支撑的规范。其功率和性能估计的精度可达 1–5%，它大约比 RTL 模拟快 200 倍，且可通过 ‘contracts’ 正式验证。

In every silicon program to date, human architects have written many English PDFs before handing off to an implementation team and a verification team. However, natural language cannot capture every detail an implementation needs precisely and unambiguously, and it cannot guarantee that every agent hallucination is caught while the ASIC is being designed and verified. Natural language was never built for this, and in a world where AI writes the specification, we opt for a formal, machine-checkable specification language instead.

在每个 silicon program 迄今为止，人类 architects 已经编写了许多 English PDFs，然后交付给 implementation team 和 verification team。然而， natural language 不能精确且明确地捕获 implementation 需要的每一个细节，也不能保证在 ASIC 设计和验证期间捕获每个 agent hallucination。

ASL can formally describe both high-level, protocol-like behavior, such as out-of-order handling, CSR programming, memory ordering, and coherency, and low-level details, such as pipelines, arbitration mechanisms, and compute transfer functions. This lets the model leave the specification open-ended where that is useful and constrain it exactly where a precise behavior is required. RTL and alignment

RTL 与对齐

Because ASL is a formally backed specification, designing and verifying the RTL derived from it is the fastest part of the entire Frostbite process. Arcmodel, however, is not physically aware, so its power and performance estimates at first diverge from the true numbers of the timing-converged, synthesis-clean RTL, in the worst case by almost 250%.

由于 ASL 是一份有正式支持的规范，从中派生的 RTL 设计和验证是整个 Frostbite 流程中最快的部分。然而，Arcmodel 并不具备物理感知能力，因此其最初的功耗和性能估计与时序收敛、综合干净的 RTL 的真实数值存在差异，最坏情况下差异几乎达到 250%。

Before continuing the ASL autoresearch, one of our systems recalibrates Arcmodel against the RTL. This is a fully autonomous pipeline. It first identifies the power hotspots in the RTL and traces them down to key counters in the formal specification, such as SRAM reads and writes, operation counts, flits sent and received, credit returns, and frame misses. The model may then write any scalar Python function over those counters to predict power, and it repeats this process until the RTL and Arcmodel agree to within 5%.

在继续 ASL autoresearch 之前，我们的某个系统会针对 RTL 重新校准 Arcmodel。这完全是一个自主流水线。它首先会识别出 RTL 中的功率热点，并将它们追踪至形式规范中的关键计数器，例如 SRAM 的读写，操作计数，flits 的发送与接收，信用返回以及帧丢失。随后，模型可能会在这些计数器上编写任何标量 Python 函数来预测功率，并重复这一过程，直到 RTL 与 Arcmodel 在 5% 以内达成一致。

We find this style of non-gradient learning extremely powerful. Once this first physical alignment has been applied, later iterations are much faster. These are, of course, still pre-silicon power numbers, and over multiple tapeout loops, ASL models can be correlated to true post-silicon, production power numbers.

Architectural novelty

架构新颖性

The architecture in full detail would warrant its own post. Instead, we choose to focus here on the features that we considered either novel or creative and highlight the capability of our systems to push the frontiers of hardware design.

该架构的完整细节足以另起一篇文章。因此，我们在此重点介绍那些我们认为新颖或富有创意的特性，并凸显我们的系统在拓展硬件设计前沿方面的能力。

Programs for Frostbite are written in Vine,2 which is a fully fledged programming language with syntax similar to Rust. A Vine program is compiled to Ivy, an intermediate representation (IR) that encodes the interaction net structure. The optimizer also tries to apply as many of the graph reduction rules as it can, so the final Ivy net, as it is called, has a (mostly) fixed shape, composed of three primitives: data, computation nodes, and control nodes. However, the runtime of this net is still very dynamic, because unlike the typical computation graph, where the parallelism is encoded in the structure and pipelined over time, the parallelism has to be derived at runtime from the state and pipelined spatially. The initial naïve implementations were slow, so our agents had to get creative.

程序为 Frostbite 编写于 Vine,2，它是一门语法类似 Rust 的完整的编程语言。一个 Vine 程序编译为 Ivy，一个中间表示 (IR) 编码交互网结构。优化器也试图应用尽可能多的 graph reduction rules，所以称为 Ivy net 的最终 (mostly) 固定的形状，由 data、计算节点和控制节点三个原语组成。然而，这 net 的运行时仍然 very 动态，因为与典型的 computation graph 不同，后者将并行性编码在结构中并随时间流水线化，并行性必须从运行时的 state 中推导并流水线 spatially。最初的 naïve 实现都很慢，所以我们的代理不得不发挥创意。

The generated ISA follows from this set of constraints. A lot of it is expected: wide bundles, hardware loop counters, and streams. We found the dynamic features more interesting, particularly operations to take, peek, and copy values from other parts of the net that would be running in parallel. The tiles then come alive, communicating across space.

生成的 ISA 源于这组约束。其中大部分是意料之中的：宽捆绑、硬件循环计数器和流。我们发现动态特性更加有趣，尤其是从网络其他并行运行的部分获取、窥视和复制值的操作。随后，瓦片活跃起来，跨空间进行通信。

Fig. 7. Code-to-hardware on Frostbite. The first call populates the chip, and then the calls it makes follow it, reusing the same nodes in a recursive fashion, until every tile is firing at once. The recursion is spread across space.

Fig. 7. Code-to-hardware on Frostbite. 首次调用填充芯片，随后的调用随之而来，以递归方式重用相同的节点，直到每个瓷片同时激活。递归跨越空间。

Emergent property: stealing work

涌现属性 (emergent property): 盗取工作

Because the parallelism is spread over space, there is no central scheduler. Instead, we saw the agents design these elegant rules for propagating the work. A tile follows three rules: it runs its own work first, meaning work in its input ports. If those are empty, it takes work from a neighboring tile that has work to spare. If no such tile is found, it can just go inactive and save power.

由于并行性分布在空间上，因此没有中央调度器。相反，我们看到了 Agent 设计了这些优雅的规则来传播工作。每个 tile 遵循三条规则：它首先执行自己的工作，即输入端口中的工作。如果这些端口为空，它会从有富余工作的相邻 tile 中获取工作。如果没有找到这样的 tile，它可以直接进入非活动状态以节省功耗。

The agents demonstrated remarkable sophistication in how they implemented this. Below, we have the hardware for a single Frostbite tile:

Agent 在实现这一点的方式上展现出了非凡的精巧。以下是单个 Frostbite tile 的硬件：

Fig. 8. A Frostbite tile. The bounding boxes demonstrate how to think about the domains of the blocks.

Fig. 8. 一个 Frostbite 瓦片。 边界框展示了如何思考块的域。

A lot of them should be familiar. We are interested in the RUNTIME domain that is responsible for the work-stealing behavior described above.

其中很多应该都很熟悉。我们关注 RUNTIME 域，它负责上述描述的 work-stealing 行为。

The compiler breaks code into short sections that run uninterrupted once their inputs are ready. These are run in the engine and are mostly organized like traditional computation through the front end. Whenever a loop or branch splits into parallel pieces whose sizes aren’t known ahead of time, the running section parks whatever comes after into a small record in local memory, the frame manager. It then drops the new tasks onto a hardware queue called the work queue and picks up the newest one itself. Idle neighbors are then free to pull the remaining tasks over the network. As tasks finish anywhere on the chip in any order, their return packets tick down the parked record’s counter and automatically wake the next section the instant the last piece arrives.

编译器将代码拆分为多个短代码段，这些代码段在输入就绪后便会不间断运行。它们在 engine 中执行，且主要通过 front end 以传统计算方式组织。每当循环或分支拆分出多个并行片段、且其大小无法预先确定时，正在运行的代码段会将后续部分暂存到本地内存中的一条小记录里，即 frame manager。随后，它将新任务推入名为 work queue 的硬件队列，并自行拾取最新的一个任务执行。此时，空闲的邻近单元便可通过网络拉取剩余任务。当芯片上任意位置的任务按任意顺序完成后，其返回包会递减暂存记录的计数器，并在最后一片到达的那一刻自动唤醒下一个代码段。

This is what it looks like in hardware:

这在硬件中看起来像：

Fig. 9. How tiles share a workload.

图 9. 瓦片如何共享工作负载

We can think of each “task” as the current board, one level down, with one more queen. Tile 0 has to queue three tasks for all the possible queen configurations before it can finish the present board state. It’s free, so it takes the newest task (from itself) and runs it. Meanwhile, its neighbors have gotten the other ones, except for Tile 5, which goes back to sleep.

我们可以将每个“任务”视为当前棋盘向下一级且包含一个额外的皇后。Tile 0 必须为所有可能的皇后配置将三个任务排队，然后才能完成当前的棋盘状态。由于它空闲，它会取出最新的任务（来自自身）并执行。与此同时，它的邻居节点已获取了其他任务，只有 Tile 5 重新进入休眠状态。

This behavior was never specified by any human. We can directly trace it back to necessity on specific regressions and hill-climbing performance metrics.

这种行为从未由任何人类规定。我们可以将其直接追溯至修复特定回归和优化爬山性能指标的必要性。

Results

结果

We synthesized Frostbite on a 7 nm process, reaching 800 MHz timing at synthesis and 500 MHz in the final GDS. Each Frostbite quad (a two-by-two grid of tiles) paired with four L3 nodes is 0.792 mm². We benchmark one Quad+L3 cluster against a single core of a modern superscalar (dual-issue, in-order) CPU, which we refer to as TCPU (“Traditional CPU”). This TCPU is 0.895 mm² at the same process.†

我们在 7 nm 工艺上合成了 Frostbite，综合时序达到 800 MHz，最终 GDS 中为 500 MHz。每个 Frostbite quad（一个 two-by-two 的 tiles 网格）配备四个 L3 nodes，面积为 0.792 mm²。我们将一个 Quad+L3 cluster 与现代超标量（dual-issue, in-order）CPU 的单核进行基准测试，我们将其称为 TCPU（“Traditional CPU”）。该 TCPU 在相同工艺下的面积为 0.895 mm²。†

Fig. 10. Frostbite layout, four by four tiles, on a 7 nm process, with one Frostbite quad (two by two tiles) and one L3 node outlined.

图 10. Frostbite 布局，4×4 tiles，基于 7 nm 工艺，其中一个 Frostbite quad（2×2 tiles）和一个 L3 node 被框出。

We benchmarked on a wide set of workloads, from dense, parallel kernels such as gemm and conv2d, to irregular, branching programs such as JSON parsing, Huffman coding, k-d trees, and recursive Fibonacci. A search set of workloads drove all architectural optimization, ISA design, RTL, and verification, and the chip was evaluated on both the 10 search-set workloads and the 15 held out, including the five practical workloads added later (Fig. 3).

我们在广泛的工作负载上进行了基准测试，从密集的并行内核（如 gemm 和 conv2d）到不规则的分支程序（如 JSON 解析、 Huffman 编码、 k-d 树和递归 Fibonacci）。搜索集工作负载驱动了所有架构优化、 ISA 设计、 RTL 和验证，该芯片在 10 个搜索集工作负载和 15 个保留工作负载上都进行了评估，其中包括后来添加的五个实际工作负载（图 3）。

For a fair comparison, we chose to first measure “single-core” performance by benchmarking one Frostbite quad against the TCPU, since they have similar area. Across all the workloads, we average an 8.77x performance-per-area, and across all 25 workloads, search set and held out together, Frostbite reaches a geometric mean of 4.59x the TCPU’s performance-per-watt: 6.02x on the 10 search-set workloads, and 3.83x on the 15 held-out workloads it was never tuned on. As expected, the architecture does most strongly on highly parallelizable tasks, but it also outperforms the TCPU on branching, dynamic code.

为了进行公平比较，我们首先选择测量“单核”性能，即将一个 Frostbite 四核组与 TCPU 进行基准测试，因为二者面积相近。在所有工作负载中，我们实现了平均 8.77 倍的性能密度（performance-per-area）优势，而在全部 25 个工作负载（搜索集与保留集合计）上，Frostbite 达到了 TCPU 性能功耗比（performance-per-watt）几何平均值的 4.59 倍：在 10 个搜索集工作负载上为 6.02 倍，在从未调优过的 15 个保留集工作负载上为 3.83 倍。正如预期，该架构在高度可并行化任务上表现最强，但在分支密集、动态代码上也优于 TCPU。

Fig. 11. Performance-per-watt of one Frostbite quad relative to the TCPU’s best build, across 25 workloads: the 10 in the search set, and the 15 in the held-out eval set. Dashed lines mark the geometric mean of the eval set, of all 25, and of the search set.

图 11. 一个 Frostbite quad 相对于 CPU 的最佳版本在 25 个工作负载上的性能每瓦：其中 10 个在搜索集中，15 个在保留评估集中。虚线标记了评估集、全部 25 个工作负载以及搜索集的几何平均值。

Fig. 12. Share of each chip’s energy by function, excluding clock distribution, for the TCPU, one Frostbite quad, and the full four-by-four Frostbite. Mean over 20 workloads.

Fig. 12. TCPU、单个 Frostbite quad 和完整的四乘四 Frostbite 按功能划分的各芯片能量占比（不包括时钟分发）。20 个 workloads 的平均值。

The energy breakdown shows where the savings come from. Leaving out clock distribution (49% of TCPU energy, 41% of a Frostbite quad’s), the TCPU spends 57% of its energy on memory and 27% on fetching, decoding, and issuing instructions. Frostbite cuts memory to 38% and fetch, decode, and issue to just 6%. In exchange, it spends 26% on its on-chip network and scheduler, the cost of sharing work and moving messages between tiles. What’s more exciting, however, is that as we scale the chip to a four-by-four array (four quads), the power distribution is relatively the same. In a general-purpose multi-core CPU arrangement, scaling the number of cores requires adding heavy coherency mechanisms and large caches, whereas when running interaction nets, the same data locality rules always apply, and more cores do not increase system complexity. This is illustrated below. In the coming months, we’ll be benchmarking Frostbite mesh-like configurations against multi-core “TCPU” arrangements with large caches and larger, wider, out-of-order CPUs, over a larger set of industry benchmarks such as SPEC and PARSEC.

能耗分析揭示了节能的来源。不考虑时钟分发（占 TCPU 能耗的 49%，Frostbite quad 的 41%），TCPU 将 57% 的能耗用于内存，27% 用于取指、译码和指令发射。Frostbite 将内存能耗降至 38%，取指、译码和发射降至仅 6%。作为交换，它将 26% 用于片上网络和调度器，这是在瓦片之间共享工作和传递消息的代价。更令人兴奋的是，当我们将芯片扩展为四乘四阵列（四个 quads）时，功耗分布基本相同。在通用多核 CPU 架构中，扩展核心数量需要添加沉重的一致性机制和大容量缓存；而在运行 interaction nets 时，相同的数据局部性规则始终适用，更多核心并不会增加系统复杂性。如下图所示。在未来几个月，我们将把 Frostbite 类网状配置与具有大容量缓存以及更大、更宽、乱序 CPU 的多核“TCPU”架构进行基准测试，测试集包括更广泛的行业基准，如 SPEC 和 PARSEC。

Fig. 13. Where the memory sits. A multi-core TCPU shares a deep hierarchy of L1, L2, and L3 caches across its cores; Frostbite gives every tile its own small memory. Schematic, not to scale.

图 13. 内存的位置。多核 TCPU 在其核心之间共享一个深层的 L1、L2 和 L3 缓存层次结构；Frostbite 为每个 tile 提供各自的小容量内存。示意图，不按比例绘制。

What comes next

接下来的内容

While interaction nets have been around for more than 35 years, their production value has never been fully clear. Historically, there has always been a risk of exploring out-of-distribution architectures, for the time, investment, and labor required to come to conviction. We believe AI fundamentally changes these economics. In the search for higher performance and lower power, extreme co-design of workloads, ISA, and hardware will continue to be demanded. With large agent swarms, sophisticated search-space techniques, precise guardrails, formal verification, and faster EDA tools, AI systems will be able to discover and build novel accelerators at a quality that exceeds human cognition. While there is much more to do, we feel it is the right time to share with the world what the future of autonomous chip design could look like. We plan to continue scaling development on Frostbite, including but not limited to:

交互网络已存在超过 35 年，但其产值始终不明确。历史上，始终存在探索 out-of-distribution 架构的风险，因为在当时所需的时间、投资和人力以达到确信。我们相信 AI 根本改变了这些经济。在追求 higher performance 和 更低 power 的过程中，极端的 workload 、ISA 和 hardware 协同设计 将继续被要求。随着大规模 agent swarms、精密的 search-space 技术、精确的 guardrails、形式化验证以及更快的 EDA 工具，AI 系统将能够发现并构建新型 accelerators 质量超过人类认知。虽然还有许多工作需要完成， 但我们觉得现在是向世界展示自主 chip design 未来的合适时机。我们计划继续在 Frostbite 上进行规模化开发， 包括 但不限于：

  • Deliver a software playground for anybody to run a program on Frostbite, hosted on FPGAs.
  • Build a preliminary operating system capable of managing hardware resources, multiple programs, virtualization, and more.
  • Scale swarms to bring Frostbite to higher performance-per-watt, and benchmark it on a much larger set of workloads against a broader set of CPUs.
  • Release the RTL and ISA for Frostbite.
  • 提供一个软件试验平台，让任何人都能在托管于 FPGA 上的 Frostbite 上运行程序。
  • 构建一个初步的操作系统，能够管理硬件资源、多个程序、虚拟化等。
  • 扩展 swarm 规模，以将 Frostbite 提升至更高的性能功耗比，并在更大规模的工作负载集合上、针对更广泛的 CPU 集合进行基准测试。
  • 发布 Frostbite 的 RTL 和 ISA。

We are having a lot of fun!

我们玩得很开心！

Notes

笔记

† For legal reasons, we cannot disclose the exact CPU.

† 由于法律原因，我们无法披露确切的 CPU。

参考文献

Partner with us

与我们合作

If your edge depends on the silicon underneath it, whether you’re an AI lab, a fabless chip company, an OEM, a defense prime, or ASIC design partner, we want to hear from you.

如果你的优势依赖于底层的硅，无论你是 AI 实验室、无晶圆厂芯片公司、OEM、国防主承包商，还是 ASIC 设计合作伙伴，我们都希望听到你的声音。

item.content:encoded:
from: If you can’t explain something in simple terms, you don’t understand it

In the early 1960s, Richard Feynman gave a series of undergraduate lectures that were collected into a book called the Feynman Lectures on Physics. Absent from the book was a lecture Feynman gave on planetary motion, but a later finding of the notes enabled David Goodstein, a colleague of Feynman’s, to write a book about it: Feynman’s Lost Lecture. From an excerpt of the book published in a 1996 issue of Caltech’s Engineering & Science magazine:

在 1960 年代早期，Richard Feynman 给出了一系列本科讲座，这些讲座被收录成一本名为 the Feynman Lectures on Physics 的书。然而，这本书中缺失了一篇关于行星运动的讲座，a lecture 但随后对讲义的发现使得 David Goodstein，一位 Feynman 的同事，能够写出关于它的书籍：Feynman’s Lost Lecture。以下摘录来自 1996 年 《Caltech’s Engineering & Science》杂志的刊物（ http://calteches.library.caltech.edu/563/2/Goodstein.pdf）：

Feynman was a truly great teacher. He prided himself on being able to devise ways to explain even the most profound ideas to beginning students. Once, I said to him, “Dick, explain to me, so that I can understand it, why spin one-half particles obey Fermi-Dirac statistics.” Sizing up his audience perfectly, Feynman said, “I’ll prepare a freshman lecture on it.” But he came back a few days later to say, “I couldn’t do it. I couldn’t reduce it to the freshman level. That means we don’t really understand it.”

费曼是一位真正伟大的教师。他总是为自己能够设计出让初学者理解最深奥概念的方法而自豪。有一次，我对他说：“迪克，向我解释一下，让我能理解，为什么自旋为 1/2 的粒子遵循费米-狄拉克统计。”费曼准确判断了听众的水平，回答道：“我会准备一场关于这个主题的大一讲座。”但几天后他回来告诉我：“我做不到。我无法将它降低到大一学生的理解水平。这意味着我们并没有真正理解它。”

John Gruber writes the simple explanations are the goal at Apple as well:

John Gruber 写了 简单的解释也是 Apple 的目标：

Engineers are expected to be able to explain a complex technology or product in simple, easily-understood terms not because the executive needs it explained simply to understand it, but as proof that the engineer understands it completely.

工程师之所以要能用简单易懂的语言解释复杂的技术或产品，并非因为高管需要简单的解释才能听懂，而是作为工程师彻底理解该技术的证明。

Feynman was well known for simple explanations of scientific concepts that result a in deeper understanding of the subject matter: e.g. see Feynman explaining how fire is stored sunshine, rubber bands, how trains go around curves, and magnets. Critically, he’s also not shy about admitting when he doesn’t understand something…or, alternately, when scientists as a group don’t understand something. There’s the spin anecdote above and of his explanation of magnets, he says:

费曼以简单解释科学概念而闻名，这种解释带来对主题的更深入理解：例如，看看费曼如何解释 how fire is stored sunshine, rubber bands, how trains go around curves, 和 magnets. 关键在于，他也不吝啬承认自己某事不懂，或者，换一种说法，当科学家们作为一个群体时不明白某事。 上面的 spin 轶事以及他 his explanation of magnets 的解释，他说道：

I really can’t do a good job, any job, of explaining magnetic force in terms of something else you’re more familiar with, because I don’t understand it in terms of anything else you’re more familiar with.

我真的无法用你更熟悉的任何事物来说好磁力的解释，因为我自己也并不理解磁力究竟是以什么为基础的。

Feynman was also quoted as saying:

费曼也曾被引述说：

I think I can safely say that nobody understands quantum mechanics.

我认为我可以安全地说，没有人理解量子力学。

Pretty interesting thing to hear from a guy who won a Nobel Prize for explaining quantum mechanics better than anyone ever had before. Even when he died in 1988 at the end of a long and fruitful careeer, a note at the top of his blackboard read:

能从一个因以前所未有地更好地解释 quantum mechanics 而荣获 Nobel Prize 的人那里听到这话，颇为有趣。即使在他 1988 年辞世时，漫长而硕果累累的职业生涯已近尾声，他 黑板 顶端的一张便条上写着：

What I cannot create, I do not understand.

我无法创造的，我便不理解。

item.title: 急速公告：Alessandro Masullo GRH
item.description:
Hi everyone,

大家好，

I am at the American Mathematical Society Executive Committee and Board of Trustees meeting now, and about to chair an hours-long meeting, but this is urgent, so I will try to get this out quickly. Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of GRH, and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. It is all human, with no AI. The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people. Now it seems best to put out the current draft. I hope people quickly check it, formalize, fill any small gaps if they occur. I really hope it works. I have great faith in Brian’s judgement, and Brian has put a lot of thought into checking what Alessandro has done. There is a long story to tell, but right now I want to get the file out. Here it is.
item.content:encoded:
from: Hurried Announcement: Alessandro Masullo GRH

Hi everyone,

大家好，

I am at the American Mathematical Society Executive Committee and Board of Trustees meeting now, and about to chair an hours-long meeting, but this is urgent, so I will try to get this out quickly. Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of GRH, and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. It is all human, with no AI. The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people. Now it seems best to put out the current draft. I hope people quickly check it, formalize, fill any small gaps if they occur. I really hope it works. I have great faith in Brian’s judgement, and Brian has put a lot of thought into checking what Alessandro has done. There is a long story to tell, but right now I want to get the file out. Here it is.

我正在美国数学学会（AMS）执行委员会和受托人委员会开会，马上就要主持一场持续数小时的会议，但这事紧急，所以我得赶紧发这条消息。
